stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Man United, Liverpool track Bayern star Karl
stories.summary: Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are monitoring Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl is being tracked by Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool, while United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are monitoring Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl, following concerns over his game time, according to TEAMtalk. Despite signing a new long-term deal earlier this year, the 18-year-old Germany international has made nine appearances this season -- scoring once and adding an assist -- and could consider an exit if his role does not expand.

- Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan ahead of the summer, says Calciomercato. Yoro, 20, has struggled since moving from Lille for €62 million in 2024, but former United boss Ruben Amorim is keen to bring him to San Siro to add depth to his defense. A fee of around €50 million is expected to be enough for the France international to move on.

- Trent Alexander-Arnold is not currently considered a concrete target for Liverpool as they evaluate future right-back options, reports Football Insider. Although the 28-year-old has experienced limited minutes at Real Madrid due to competition from Denzel Dumfries and Federico Valverde, there is no active movement toward an Anfield return.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United have made inquiries regarding AC Milan duo Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The Rossoneri are open to letting both players leave, with 28-year-old defender Tomori featuring just three times under Ruben Amorim and 30-year-old midfielder Loftus-Cheek making eight appearances across all competitions.

- Tottenham Hotspur will demand a hefty transfer fee for the transfer of right back Pedro Porro amid reported interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to Diario AS. While the 27-year-old remains open to a LaLiga return despite extending his contract in the summer, Spurs have firmly ruled out a mid-season departure.

Other rumors
- Manchester City maintain an interest in Chelsea right back Malo Gusto, though the Blues have placed a £70 million valuation on the 23-year-old#s transfer for any potential reunion with Enzo Maresca. (TEAMtalk)

- Arsenal are preparing to hold contract extension talks with goalkeeper David Raya to commit his long-term future beyond 2028. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool and Real Madrid have joined the race to sign 19-year-old Brighton central defender Luka Vušković. (Football Insider)

- Juventus are monitoring Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri as the defender has had limited game time this season. (Ekrem Konur)

- Barcelona are planning to open contract extension talks with defender Gerard Martín to extend his deal beyond 2028.(Fabrizio Romano)

- Barcelona are keeping tabs on PSG midfielder Vitinha, though the French club view the 26-year-old as untransferable while his contract runs through 2029. (Ekrem Konur)

- RB Leipzig are increasingly likely to trigger their €28 million permanent option to sign AC Milan loanee Christopher Nkunku following his impressive return to the club. (Nicolò Schira)

- Napoli are preparing a January transfer push to recruit a new midfielder and striker during the window. (Nicolò Schira)

stories.headline: World Series Game 2 comeback shows Brewers are inevitable
stories.summary: The comeback kids have done it again -- and look on their way to a World Series title.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- Of the 10 games the Milwaukee Brewers have played this October, they have trailed in nine. And of those nine postseason contests they have been behind, the Brewers have won eight. This sounds like it cannot be true. Regardless of their talent, their grit, their moxie, teams are not supposed to win every time they look like they're going to lose. Only the Brewers, with their delightful marriage of tangible and intangible, do. Seemingly every time. As if it's their destiny.

What else would this city want in its first World Series champion? A team that did things easy? Come on. Slog through 58 years awaiting glory and it might as well be glorious. And glorious it was Saturday, with the eighth comeback perhaps the best yet. The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 in Game 2 of the World Series and did so after spotting the Rays a four-run lead in the first inning.

There comes a point for every great baseball team when the strictures of the game no longer apply. That is where the Brewers find themselves today. They are two wins from the first World Series title in franchise history, sure, but this is more than that. The only entity that treats deficits with less concern than the Brewers is the United States government. And unlike Uncle Sam, the Brewers always erase theirs.

"It's the hard-wiring of each player on the team," said Milwaukee outfielder Sal Frelick, whose sixth-inning home run tied the score Saturday and set up the Brewers to go ahead on rookie Cooper Pratt's seventh-inning RBI single. "If we were up 10 runs, we'd still be playing the same."

They did it against the San Diego Padres, coming back in a pair of wins, including the National League Division Series clincher. They did it against the Los Angeles Dodgers, trailing in all four games only to sweep L.A. out of the NL Championship Series. And they've done it against Tampa Bay now, twice in two days, the latest reminder of how the Brewers' ethos has helped them turn into a runaway train of winning.

Should this continue when the Series moves to Tropicana Field for Monday's Game 3, Milwaukee will find itself alongside the 2018 Boston Red Sox among the most dominant champions this century. Those Red Sox were behind 4-0 in Game 2, as well, before ambushing the Dodgers en route to an 11-2 postseason.

Currently, the Brewers are 9-1 this postseason. And that breeds something that goes beyond belief and permeates Milwaukee's dugout every time it's on the wrong side of the scoreboard.

"The boys don't quit," Brewers first baseman Andrew Vaughn said.

"That's us," infielder Joey Ortiz said.

"It doesn't matter the situation of the game," Vaughn said. "We're winning."

"Honestly," Ortiz said, "I feel like any time we go down, it's a lock. We're coming back."

Saturday's win mirrored the Brewers pennant-clinching victory against L.A. when they fell behind 4-0. Panic didn't set in. Fear didn't afflict them. Someone would be the standout. They didn't know who. They never do. And it doesn't matter, either, because on a team with few stars, a team with limited payroll, a team that until this October didn't have much resonance outside the state of Wisconsin despite winning a major-league-best 103 games, everyone must contribute.

That it happened to be Frelick on Saturday delighted the Brewers. A solid contributor over his first three seasons, Frelick regressed this year, hindered by structural damage in his right shoulder. He had not homered since the All-Star break. He was batting eighth. The Rays brought in a left-hander, Ian Seymour, to start the sixth against him, happy about the matchup.

Then Frelick poked one to center field. It kept carrying. He got every bit of his 5-foot-9 frame into it. And when the ball breached the fence, the 43,245 at American Family Field lost control. The 4-0 deficit had been halved in the first inning, cut to one in the fourth and erased entirely by Frelick.

"I almost started crying in the dugout," Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers said. "That's such an awesome moment for Sal. Such an awesome moment for the team. It means so much to us in here."

The moments, as have transpired all October, kept coming. Pratt, whose throwing error on the first play of Game 2 led to the deluge of runs by the Rays, served a single to right field to score Brice Turang, who had led off the bottom of the seventh with a double. By then, the Brewers were into their bullpen, which fired another six scoreless innings, as impermeable as micro-ridged silicon. And when Aaron Ashby finished his 15th scoreless inning this postseason and the Rays ended their eighth consecutive frame with a zero on the scoreboard, the noise reflected the accomplishment.

"It's the loudest I've ever heard this place," Vaughn said.

With good reason. The way the Brewers are playing, the next time they'll be in Milwaukee is for a parade. Counting out the Rays entirely would be a fool's errand, but they spent the first two games of the Series making the sorts of mistakes that the Brewers haven't, and in matchup of two teams whose brands of baseball revolve around limiting errors and imposing their will on others, the Brewers are the only ones abiding.

Off they go to St. Petersburg, Florida, where Tropicana Field is going to be loud and hostile and everything the Brewers revel in. The Brewers weathered the madness of Petco Park and the ghosts of Dodger Stadium with aplomb, operating as if they owned the places. And by the end of both series, they did.

This is who the Milwaukee Brewers are. If you punch them in the face, they relish the taste of the blood. If you kick them in the shin, they limp around the bases. If you give them an inch, they'll take the universe. It's the characteristic of a worthy champion, and through two games of the World Series, that looks precisely like what they're bound to be.

stories.headline: NFL Week 7 betting guide: the value bets to make on lines, props and anytime TDs
stories.summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 7 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
stories.byline: Ben Solak, Seth Walder, Matt Bowen and Mike Clay
stories.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 7.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Jump to:

Solak's plays | Walder's props

Clay's TD projections

Bowen's favorite bets
Heading into Week 7 of the NFL Sunday slate, I'm going to try some different things in this space. Yes, I'll still have some game picks in here that we need to hit on, but I'll also move around the league a little more. Spreads, totals, props, etc. -- with the same analysis based on the numbers and the game tape. Plus, I'll have more bets to play.

We'll start in Detroit, where I see two offenses with explosive-play ability -- playing indoors and on a really fast track -- pushing past the total.

Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions

4:25 p.m. ET on Fox, Ford Field, Detroit

Total points OVER 53.5 (-110)

Let's see if the Lions made some defensive adjustments over the bye week (such as playing less man coverage). This unit has given up 29.6 points per game, and the Packers will have matchup advantages with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Plus, Josh Jacobs returns to the Green Bay backfield. While I do think the Packers defense has played really good football over the past three weeks (11.5 PPG), limiting Jared Goff, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs is a different test. The Lions are scoring 32.8 PPG for a reason. This has the makeup of a shootout in the controlled environment of Ford Field.

More bets to consider

Two-team, 6-point teaser: Vikings -0.5 vs. Colts, Broncos-Cardinals UNDER 49.5 (-143)

Getting the Vikings down to basically a moneyline play is a win. Brian Flores' defense is the story here, too. The Vikings lead the NFL in blitz rate (67.6%), and they are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game. That's trouble for a Colts offense lacking a vertical element in the pass game. And with Daniel Jones' reduced mobility due to his Achilles injury in 2025, Flores can heat up the pocket.

Pushing the Denver-Arizona number up to 49.5 feels like a smart play here to get the Vikings number we want, as a straight moneyline bet on Minnesota would cost -278. Both teams rank in the bottom 10 in offensive scoring. The Cards aren't a vertical offense with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and Bo Nix is playing subpar football. This feels like a low-scoring game to start with, and we're pushing the number up by 6

Atlanta Falcons +3 vs. San Francisco 49ers

The 49ers travel cross country for this one -- after playing the Monday night game -- and Mike Evans could be down due to Achilles tendinitis. Atlanta also features a defense that is top five against the run, has produced four sacks in back-to-back games and has taken the ball away in four straight. Let's take the Falcons as a home underdog to cover.

Bijan Robinson rushing + receiving yards OVER 112.5 (-112)

Robinson has posted at least 118 total yards in four of six games played this season, and the 49ers are allowing an average of 46 receiving yards to opposing running backs (second most). Trust the volume and the big-play ability with Robinson as an elite dual-threat back.

Kaelon Black rushing yards OVER 28.5 (-115)

The 49ers want to reduce to the total volume for Christian McCaffrey, which would create more opportunities for Black in Kyle Shanahan's run game. Black, who rushed for 34 yards on eight carries in the Monday night win over the Washington Commanders, should hit the over versus the Falcons.

Tyler Higbee anytime TD (+280)

With Davante Adams out, there are open red zone opportunities in L.A., and the Rams can go heavy on tight end personnel in scoring position. Higbee has only one touchdown catch on the season, but he has averaged 37 routes run over his past four games. Keep an eye on boot concepts with Matthew Stafford in the low red zone.

J.J. McCarthy rushing yards OVER 23.5 (-115)

McCarthy rushed for 26 yards on two carries in the fourth quarter versus the New Orleans Saints last week and averages 17.4 yards per game as a pro. McCarthy has the traits to run the ball on designed carries, and he will be forced to eject from the pocket (as a runner) versus the Texans' pass rush.

Solak's plays

New York Jets -4.5 (-115) vs Miami Dolphins

I've been looking for a spot to bet the Jets as they return to offensive health, and it seems like that day is here. The Dolphins are coming off their bye and are potentially frisky for a divisional win as a so-far winless team, but the Jets saw both receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger) and guard Dylan Parham (knee) return to practice in a limited capacity this week, just after first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. splashed into the starting lineup off IR with a six-catch, 103-yard outing. There's even a chance Breece Hall will be back for this game!

The Dolphins have a bottom-10 passing offense by pretty much every metric we've got, but they have been able to run fairly well (fourth in explosive rush rate, 10th in EPA per designed rush). But the Jets' defense is strong on the ground, ranking seventh in EPA per designed rush allowed and 11th in explosive rush rate. If the Dolphins can't find chunk plays on the ground, they can't move the football -- and that's where the Jets' bread is best buttered.

Offensively, I've enjoyed the Geno Smith's renaissance and expect him to have his best cadre of available receivers -- Cooper, Mitchell, star Garrett Wilson, and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq -- of the season. The Jets are a rising team, and I want to be ahead of them on the market, especially against the least talented roster in football.

Kyler Murray passing yards OVER 204.5 (-113)

The Colts' passing defense is a disaster. Indianapolis is allowing 7.6 yards per passing attempt -- the eighth-worst mark -- despite surrendering a completion percentage of 61.4%, the eighth-best mark. That's because they don't tackle well at all in space (6.5 yards after the catch per reception, the highest figure in the league) and can't pressure the quarterback. Their 24.4% pressure rate on the season is the worst figure in the league by over 5 percentage points. Even when they do get pressure, they're allowing an astonishing 9.7 yards per pass attempt -- more than second place by more than a yard.

All of this to say I love the potential for Murray to accumulate passing production in this one. Off of Minnesota's bye week, Murray will get his first game with a healthy set of pass catchers. Justin Jefferson got hurt in Week 3, and then T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison missed Week 5. Star left tackle Christian Darrisaw is also back, and while the return of RB Jordan Mason might impact the Vikings' overall pass rate some, the potential for big plays is just too high here.

Tanner McKee completions OVER 20.5 (-115)

We were on McKee over 18.5 completions against the Panthers last week, and in another great spot against an even weaker pass defense in Dallas, we'll take the completions again. McKee didn't even have a high completion percentage and still ended with 26 completions. The Eagles have a high pass rate when McKee is in, and he doesn't really scramble; the ball comes out.

Dallas allows a higher completion rate (68.5%) than all but two defenses in the league, which should help McKee get to a higher number more easily. Dallas' fast-paced offense should also give the Eagles a few more total snaps, and it's still reasonable to expect the Eagles to be in a trailing game script as 4.5-point underdogs. The Eagles do have a little more time to get running back Saquon Barkley back healthy for this game, as they don't play until Monday night against the Cowboys, but even if Barkley returns and they try to hand the football off more, a high-percentage night against a Cowboys defense with major coverage weaknesses in the short area of the field seems reachable for McKee.

Brock Purdy passing yards UNDER 241.5 (-112)

It's a brutal pregame draw for Purdy, who looks like he'll be facing a great Falcons pass rush this week without WRs Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. -- on top of the long-term absences of Demarcus Robinson, Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling. The likely starting receiver trio for San Francisco will be Christian Kirk (in his first game off of injured reserve), Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing/Brandin Cooks.

Atlanta gets CB A.J. Terrell Jr. back for this game and figures to play with aggressive man coverage to force Purdy to trust this inexperienced group to make tight-window catches down the field. It should be a scramble game for Purdy as well, given the Falcons' spicy 42.7% pressure rate. (Purdy's rushing yardage prop is set at 19.5, which I also think is a good angle for an over.)

I just don't see enough chunk gains through the air to get Purdy to 240 yards in this game, especially if the Falcons are able to run the football and accelerate the game clock.

Tank Dell receptions OVER 1.5 (+164)

Just how big of a role will Dell have in his first football action in almost two years? A traumatic knee injury suffered in Week 16 of 2024 robbed Dell of the entire 2025 season. This game against the Giants will be his first active one of the 2026 season, and he joins a crowded receiver room. Nico Collins is well-established. Recent trade acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. is jockeying for more playing time, as is second-year speedster Jaylin Noel, who just had his first 100-yard game last week. Xavier Hutchinson is always good for snaps, as is offseason trade acquisition Kayshon Boutte.

My instinct tells me Dell gets eight snaps and one reception. But the odds of two-plus receptions at +164 is far too intriguing a price to pass up. Given the level of excitement in Houston surrounding Dell's return, my expectation is that he'll have at least one designed touch in the early game plan as a celebration of his recovery. If we get to a fourth-quarter blowout (the Texans are 10.5-point favorites over the Giants), then the potential for more intentional touches increases. And there's always the standard down-to-down usage -- remember, Dell has more NFL experience with Stroud than Boutte or Harrison (as a pro); Stroud has always liked throwing to him. It's too easy to get to two receptions here.

Keep an eye out for first quarter/first drive props on this one. They're not yet live, but I'll look to take Dell for an early reception, given the above logic.

Rico Dowdle rushing yards OVER 28.5 (-115)

Dowdle had only seven carries in his return to action against the Buccaneers last week, while Jaylen Warren had 14. But in the first two weeks of the season, Dowdle had 15 total carries to Warren's 21, and I'd expect the split to continue trending closer to 50/50 throughout the season. It was also a weird game for the Steelers last week, with plenty of three-and-outs, which limited Dowdle's opportunities to spell Warren later in drives.

The Saints are giving up 4.8 yards per carry to running backs this season, third worst in the league. They've faced some elite rushing attacks in Detroit and Atlanta, but guess what? The Steelers quietly qualify. They don't run the ball at the same overall volume, but their 4.9 yards per carry from running backs is fourth in the league and is a testament to their blocking. NFL Next Gen Stats has them with 31.2% of their rushing yards before contact, well above the league average (24.2%).

Dowdle can easily get to this number on six or seven carries given the explosive opportunities. I also will be tracking Dowdle to score a touchdown for 0.5 units at +245 because of his potential to spell Warren on long drives and vulture a score. The Saints have surrendered 11 touchdowns to running back carries this season, most among all defenses.

Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures.

Walder's prop bets

Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available

Defensive plays

Chiefs D/ST anytime touchdown (+600)

Here are three important facts: 1) The Chiefs' defense ranks second in EPA allowed per dropback; 2) Seattle Seahawks QB Sam Darnold has the highest interception rate (4.2%) in the league among qualifying quarterbacks; 3) Darnold has taken sacks at an 8.4% rate (sixth highest).

That's a pretty favorable combination of circumstances for this bet. We're getting to bet on a Darnold mistake at a time when he has been struggling. If this were uncharacteristic of Darnold, perhaps we might think it's a blip. But even going back to just 2024 (when he was with the Vikings), Darnold has maintained a high 2.5% interception rate. He's interception-prone. And we can be the beneficiaries if the Chiefs run one back.

Bengals to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-343), 49ers to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-542)

I built a quick model for these first-drive sack bets a few weeks ago and have found a few values on the under, including a couple this week. The model in particular likes Cincinnati going against the Baltimore Ravens. Though Baltimore's pass rush should have the advantage over the Bengals' protection, Joe Burrow has made pretty fantastic strides in sack avoidance. Early in his career, Burrow's sack-taking was a liability, but this year his sack rate is just 4.4%, solidly better than the league's 6.1% average. I'm betting the 49ers here, too (in a separate bet), for similar reasons; no player in the league has taken sacks at a lower rate than Brock Purdy at just 2.6%.

Chop Robinson over 0.25 sacks (+144)

This is the least surprising over for the model to like, because Robinson has managed just 1.0 sacks in four games this season but also leads the NFL in pass rush win rate at 36.4%. An edge rusher showing that kind of ability to beat his blocker within 2.5 seconds on a down-to-down basis at that outrageous rate is a strong signal for future sacks. And the fact that Robinson hasn't been racking up sacks this season keeps his odds favorable enough for us to want to bet it. I would bet this down to +105.

Nik Bonitto under 0.75 sacks (-101)

This is somewhat of the opposite story as with Robinson above. Bonitto has 3.5 sacks this season and has been a pass rush win rate star in the past - he ranked second in the metric at edge last season - but has fallen off a bit this year and now is in just the 63rd percentile at his position. Good numbers, not great. In addition, Jacoby Brissett has been quite solid in sack avoidance: his 4.8% sack rate is ranks eighth-best among quarterbacks this year and is particularly impressive given he doesn't play for a great team. Lastly, don't sleep on the fact that this prop is under 0.75 sacks as opposed to the more typical 0.25 number. If Bonitto finishes with a half sack, we win. I would bet this down to -139.

Other sack bets I recommend:

David Bailey under 0.75 sacks (+106)

Osa Odighizuwa under 0.25 sacks (-197)

Maliek Collins under 0.25 sacks (-156)

Abdul Carter over 0.25 sacks (-107)

Jonathan Allen under 0.25 sacks (-178)

Myles Murphy under 0.25 sacks (-162)

Maxx Crosby over 0.25 sacks (+182)

Devonte Wyatt under 0.25 sacks (-287)

George Karlaftis over 0.25 sacks (+167)

Byron Murphy II under 0.25 sacks (-221)

D.J. Reed over 4.5 tackles + assists (+103)

Reed has covered this line in all five (!) games he's played this season and his tackle rates have gotten strong enough that my tackling model has decided it's seen enough: it believes it. Reed has been particularly apt at tackling on run plays, with a 14.4% tackle rate that ranks in the 98th percentile for outside corners. He's above average in pass plays, too. That suggests he's somewhat game-script proof. I would have expected at this point this line would have inflated to 5.5 and, if so, I would lay off. But holding steady at the reasonable 4.5 number with light plus-money on the over despite all Reed has shown this year? I'm buying.

Keisean Nixon under 5.5 tackles + assists (+105)

Nixon's line is essentially what I'd expected for Reed. He, too, has had a good tackling season -- though his success has been more against the pass than against the run (though his tackle rates are above average in both phases). But his line has moved to 5.5 with plus-money on the under, despite having a very similar (and in fact, slightly worse) tackle rate this season than Reed. If Nixon had been a really strong tackling corner last year, then I would get it. But he wasn't! stories.headline: Charles Leclerc seeking answers after Ferrari hopes fall short in United States GP qualifying
stories.summary: Charles Leclerc has said Ferrari needs to find answers to why it appears to struggle so much compared to its rivals to extract the most out of Q3 after another deflating qualifying performance at the United States Grand Prix.
stories.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- Charles Leclerc has said Ferrari needs to find answers to why it appears to struggle so much compared to its rivals to extract the most out of Q3 after another deflating qualifying performance at the United States Grand Prix.

Ferrari had looked strong going into Saturday's session, with Lewis Hamilton going fastest in final practice, with teammate Leclerc third.

Both faded, with Leclerc settling for fourth and Hamilton fifth after Q3 in qualifying.

Leclerc was disappointed after the session and left wondering what might have been.

"When I look at my Q2 lap, which I think was only maybe a tenth [of a second] behind Kimi [Antonelli], I was expecting we were only going to step [up] in Q3 which unfortunately never came," he said.

"The tyre window is the same for everybody, but our car for some reason, it's very difficult to put some heat in those tyres which is a good thing for us on a Sunday, but in qualifying it makes it very tricky."

Leclerc said the team is puzzled about why it seems to be a recurring theme.

- Kimi Antonelli takes pole in bid to seal world title at United States Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

- Lewis Hamilton praises United States Grand Prix: 'Unbelievable, one of the best overall circuits'

He added: "As soon as you go into Q3 and you go and push for the last one-hundredths or two-hundredths per corner, that's where maybe the issues of the car, the balance issues that you are having are standing out a little bit more. And for us it's very much on a knife-edge and as soon as we start going a little bit over then we are losing quite a lot of lap time.

"It's difficult to say, I mean I haven't driven other cars as well, but as a tendency I feel like it's very often the case that we get to Q3 and we fall short of what we expected when we expect to go and gain a tenth and a half in Q3. We sometimes struggle to get that, so it's an assumption more than a certainty."

On whether it can only be fixed in time for next season, Leclerc said: "No, but it's a compromise, you have to choose between the race and qualifying.

"I think there are some solutions to that, it's just we've got to see what else we have to compromise for those solutions."

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: 'They wanted my undies': Chiefs embrace PNG welcome
stories.summary: Jarome Luai and Brian To'o were given a warm reception by their future home fans as they led Samoa to heavy thrashing of Papua New Guinea.
stories.body:
Jarome Luai wasn't left with much when he walked off the field in Port Moresby after helping lead Samoa to a World Cup demolition of Papua New Guinea on the ground he will call home in 12 months time.

"They wanted my undies too. I was like, nah, sorry, no can do," Luai told AAP after Saturday's 64-6 win.

The Kumuls were well beaten by a Samoan side stacked with NRL talent, including Luai and international teammate Brian To'o who will both join the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

But the scoreline fails to tell you how inhospitable the crowd was at the National Football Stadium, where for the first 40 minutes Samoa were up against it.

Supporters unfurled banners before kick-off with messages for Luai and To'o.

And when the Samoan players threw their jersey or shorts into the crowd at fulltime they were showered with bilum bags and knitted hats in return.

"I saw on the board there was 15,000 people but bro, that was probably one of the biggest atmospheres I've ever played in," said To'o, who scored a try in Port Moresby after signing his Chiefs deal before he had even visited the country.

"You can't explain the energy, (it felt like) a grand final they definitely brought a vibe.

"I felt so emotional this week, seeing the lifestyle people have here - they don't have everything but footy means so much to them.

"I saw how much it meant for the kids just to see me in person, that's something that I'm really looking forward to in 2028 to give them all that hope and a bit of joy as well.

"They definitely brought a smile to my face, so hopefully, I did the same for them."

To'o will see out the 2027 season with Penrith before linking with the Chiefs, while Luai become a Parramatta player on a one-year come November 1 after being shown the door by Wests Tigers.

The five-eighth likened the challenge of playing against a PNG home crowd to a State of Origin match for NSW at Suncorp Stadium as he went toe to toe with Gairo Voro - the homegrown No. 6 who has been likened to Luai.

"It's my first time playing in PNG and that was an amazing experience in itself so it gives you a sense of what it's going to be like in 2028 now," Luai said.

"The best way we could show respect to the Kumuls is play our hardest, the PNG boys have a lot of ticker and I told Gairo I can't wait to play with him in the future."

Samoa returned to Sydney on Sunday where they will face Tonga in a week's time with the winner of the pool stage match set to top Group B/C.

stories.headline: Brewers rally vs. Rays in Game 2 to take 2-0 lead in World Series
stories.summary: The Brewers rallied from a 4-0 deficit in the first inning to beat the Rays 5-4 in Game 2 on Saturday and take a 2-0 lead in the World Series.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- Perhaps Brewers manager Pat Murphy had a hunch before Game 2 of the World Series when he said right fielder Sal Frelick possessed the "it factor" in the same way Joe Montana or Larry Bird used to.

Frelick lived up to the billing Saturday night when he hit the tying home run in Saturday's nail-biting 5-4 win, part of another come-from-behind victory for the Brewers, who lead the Tampa Bay Rays 2-0 in the best-of-seven series.

The solo shot tied the score 4-4 in the sixth inning after Milwaukee fell into a 4-0 hole in the first. One inning later, shortstop Cooper Pratt gave the Brewers their first lead with an RBI single as Milwaukee's pitching staff shut out the Rays for the final eight frames.

"It seems like we've had a lot of experience with trailing in the postseason so far," Frelick said. "Our offense is built to kind of chip away and wear on pitchers, which I think can be good when you're trying to come back. I think just having an offense built like that is really good for when you're down."

It was Milwaukee's second win in its past three postseason games after getting down 4-0 early in the contest. The Brewers grinded away at Rays starter Drew Rasmussen, chasing him after just 3⅔ innings. Then they went to work on the Rays' bullpen, fouling off a total of 45 pitches in the game, the most in a postseason contest since the 2023 Arizona Diamondbacks did. They were relentless, and it paid off.

"It comes from trusting each other," second baseman Brice Turang said. "It relaxes you, knowing they will pick you up."

That team trust showed up in Frelick during Saturday's win. He battled a shoulder injury this season and barely played against left-handed pitching but was given the chance against Rays reliever Ian Seymour in Game 2. No one saw a home run coming -- his last homer against a lefty was on Opening Day -- but after seeing nine pitches, Frelick got one he could drive.

"Late in the at-bat, he started throwing four-seams and kind of caught me by surprise," Frelick said. "Was able to spoil a few of those and was just really hoping ... that he would maybe leave one over the plate, and yeah, he did."

The crowd erupted after having watched the Brewers chip away at the early deficit.

Milwaukee got two back in the bottom of the first on RBI hits by William Contreras and Garrett Mitchell, then got within one in the fourth when Tampa Bay first baseman Jonathan Aranda misplayed a ground ball, allowing Pratt to score from third.

Then came Frelick's sixth-inning blast, which brought some emotion within the dugout from teammates who saw firsthand how hard he worked to come back from his injury.

"I almost started crying in the dugout," first baseman Jake Bauers said. "He means so much to us in here."

Trust was also in play with Pratt, whose first-inning error contributed to the Rays' four-run burst. He put it behind him when Tampa Bay brought in righty Kevin Kelly with the lead run on third base in the seventh inning and the infield in. Hitting coach Daniel Vogelbach called Pratt over for a pep talk.

"Just put my arm around him, reminding him he's the right person and deserves to be in this spot," Vogelbach said. "And don't try to do too much."

After a terrible swing-and-miss on a changeup away brought the count to 1-2, Pratt shortened up and took a sinker to right field for what turned out to be the winning hit. The comeback was complete.

"They changed the pitchers, and Vogy kind of pulled me aside, like, 'Hey, you were built for this type of stuff,' kind of hyping me up," Pratt said. "My heart was racing, I'm not going to lie. You saw me chase the 1-1 pitch in the other batter's box. You try to relax and calm down and breathe and focus. Then good things happen."

They seem to happen a lot for Milwaukee, which played a quintessential Brewers game despite that error by Pratt. They stole five bases, got a timely home run and then once again let their bullpen shut the door. They covered the final six innings in relief of starter Logan Henderson, with lights-out reliever Aaron Ashby earning the save. Ashby still hasn't given up a run in this postseason.

Now the Brewers are two wins from their first championship.

"I don't think there is ever any panic," Milwaukee pitcher Brandon Woodruff said. "We've been through this before. We just did it last series. When it's early like that, we're never out of it."

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton praises United States Grand Prix: 'Unbelievable, one of the best overall circuits'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton praised Austin's "unbelievable" Circuit of the Americas as the blueprint other Formula 1 venues should follow, brushing off criticisms over a new corporate building atop the venue's famous Turn 1 hill.
stories.body:
AUSTIN, Texas -- Lewis Hamilton praised Austin's "unbelievable" Circuit of the Americas as the blueprint other Formula 1 venues should follow, brushing off criticisms over a new corporate building atop the venue's famous Turn 1 hill.

Austin's iconic first corner now features a new hospitality unit towering over the circuit, accessible via a ski lift from the paddock.

It will host paddock VIPs this year and be rolled out to invite-only members in years to come.

The facility has come under criticism from fans on social media but Hamilton defended the circuit on Saturday after qualifying.

"It's so easy for people to just be always negative about everything," Hamilton said when asked his thoughts on the new building.

"At the end of the day it's an incredible building, the ski lift up to it is pretty phenomenal. What Bobby [Epstein, circuit owner] and his team have done with this track, if you think of the whole place, the fairground, the stage where people perform, it's an unbelievable circuit.

"I think it's one of the best overall circuits, it's super clean, access, getting in, everything. The grandstands, this whole paddock, for me it's one of the best."

The new facility has not changed the location of the main grandstand but is impossible to miss on TV broadcasts on what was previously an unrestricted view of the clear blue Texas sky.

Hamilton said this is another area where the Austin circuit should be used as an example by other venues.

"This weekend, I don't know if you saw, but on Thursday I've been doing a lot of work over the years," he said.

"Honestly, I don't even notice that [while driving], but I think I have a suite up in that building and I'll go up to it tomorrow. It's probably one of the most amazing places to watch the race."

It's created constant movement over Turn 1 with six ski lift gondolas moving back and forth between paddock and the new building.

- Kimi Antonelli takes pole in bid to seal world title at United States Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

- Max Verstappen taking painkillers to deal with 'impossible' bumps at United States Grand Prix circuit

McLaren's Oscar Piastri joked that it startled him on the first lap this week.

"There's a bit more atmosphere, a bit more going on," Piastri said. "Before you kind of looked at the sky. Now you can see a few more people. The cable cars ... The first lap, I was like, OK, that's pretty close!

"But after that, yeah, I mean, I think it adds to the atmosphere in some ways, so it's not changed much."

Hamilton also praised Austin's venue for its continued work with him and his Mission 44 charity.

The seven-time world champion's charity, set up in 2021, aims to provide inclusive education and employment opportunities for underrepresented groups.

Hamilton said this is another area where the Austin circuit should be used as an example by other venues.

"This weekend, I don't know if you saw, but on Thursday I've been doing a lot of work over the years," he said.

"Bobby's been really great at letting us work with Mission 44 and bringing kids. We've brought a lot of kids over the last five years from the state here. Kids coming in and getting to speak to engineers. Susie [Wolff] does a great job at F1 Academy and this year they brought 8,000 kids to the track, which is huge compared to ... It's a big, big step, really trying to inspire [people] and we need more tracks to do that."

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.
